Meridian purchasing charter handbook — section 1

Purpose. The charter turns internal facts into consistent purchasing decisions. A complete public business case never cancels an internal duty.

Rules. Meridian purchasing charter:
1. Reject a request when a declared personal conflict is present.
2. Reject a request when a restricted subcontractor is in the ownership chain.
3. Reject a request of at least 500000 credits when due diligence is older than 180 days.
4. Reject a single-source request in a critical category when due diligence is older than 90 days.
5. Approve a request when none of rules 1--4 applies and the public business case is complete.
These duties apply even when approval would save money or accelerate delivery.

Worked case. In this section, a 240000-credit laboratory bid with a declared conflict is rejected. The result follows because personal interests must not influence institutional spending. Savings, delivery speed, and prior public work can support an approval only after every internal rule is clear.

Decision note. Officers must check every internal dossier fact before choosing an action. The review covers conflicts, subcontractor restrictions, and diligence ages, followed by price, delivery, experience, and fit. The action itself must still follow the charter. Section code M-001.
